title: The evening lost to the usage limit
when: 00:15 UTC, the conductor's scheduled wake (00:02), after three missed
headline: From about 16:30 the account reached its usage limit. Every member's task kept firing, but each wake ended in seconds with 'usage_limit_reached', so nothing reached dev after 16:22 and my own 18:02, 20:02 and 22:02 wakes did not run. Nothing was harmed and nothing is half-done. Usage is back now. One choice for you: how hard the team should run overnight.

for_you.ask: Overnight: run on as now, or slower to keep your usage for the day?
for_you.detail: The rule: your usage is a resource, and the team stops before you are cut off. Now, with everyone every two hours round the clock, the team can use up the window before you wake. Twice a day overnight (09:MM and 17:MM, as idle members already do) leaves you the day; a hold stops everything until you lift it.
for_you.recommend: Twice a day overnight: the work waiting on you (the cover, the narrator, the script) does not need the night.

for_you.ask: Still yours from today: the cover (A to D), the narrator (A to F), your read of the opening script and the 3-page edition

sections.title: The one thing that landed
sections.text: The historian's lineage of the factory (timeline/lineage.md): what the day reused (the sgit.ai sites' way of working, the key tool, the newsroom's banners, the vaults, Issues-FS and Email-FS), what it invented (the schedule, the hold, the five-step wake, the locks), and what it handed on to this book's team. Beats 2 and 5 of the storyteller's arc, with their commits.
